**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The document's IP and data provisions sit at our **preferred** position:

- **Customer Data / Customer IP (§14.1, §1.3):** Customer owns all Customer Data, Confidential Information, Customer-provided material and independently developed IP; Vendor gets only a limited processing right. The definition captures derived output and carves out only telemetry that cannot be linked back to us.
- **Deliverables (§14.2, §1.4):** Customer owns each Deliverable on creation, with an express Vendor assignment of worldwide right, title and interest plus equivalent personnel assignments and further-assurances.
- **Vendor IP with licence back (§14.3 → §13.2):** Vendor retains Vendor Technology (acceptable), but embedded Vendor Technology carries a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify, create derivative works and permit contractor support — plus a duty to flag material Vendor Technology and not to embed restrictive third-party material.
- **No joint ownership / feedback (§14.4):** No joint IP unless separately signed; feedback use is limited to generalized suggestions and we keep unrestricted rights in our own feedback.
- **Data use guardrails (§15.1):** No sale, advertising use, cross-customer combination or generally available model training without our written consent — and no aggregated/derived-data grab anywhere in the document.

Nothing falls to the fallback or into walk-away territory, so no changes are warranted.
